findings.description: The new intro line in all five forms says any one-word answer counts as vague. Intake exempts its terse fields from that rule (src/core/ticket-intake.utils.ts:37,43-44,53,58,65,68), so a lone `#422` in Source PR, `2h` in Time box, or one path in Suspected area, Affected area, Files in scope or Form of the answer passes. follow-up.yml's own Source PR asks for a one-word `#NNN`, which contradicts its header. The rubrics already add 'where the field asks for a sentence'; the five form headers should say the same.

The 'an empty list item is vague' case passes because of PLACEHOLDER's `-+` branch, not the empty-list-item rule: `'- '` trims to `-`. Deleting EMPTY_LIST_ITEM in ticket-intake.utils.ts would not fail it, and the comment above it claims coverage the test lacks. Use a value such as `$'src/a.ts\n- '` so only the empty-list-item rule can flag it.

`[ -f "$file" ]` is false for a pipe, so `ticket-check.sh bug <(gh issue view 12 --json body -q .body)` is refused with 'no file at /dev/fd/63' and exit 2. `[ -r "$file" ] && [ ! -d "$file" ]` would accept it and still reject a missing path.

The Proof bullet ('the checks that exist today, tests, commands or outputs, and pass before and after without edits') reads as a garbled list. The form's wording ('Checks that exist today and pass before and after without edits: test files, commands or outputs') is clearer, and the rubric should use it.
The INTAKE_MODULE and TICKET_TYPE env vars could be positional arguments. `node -e "$check" <module> <type>` exposes them as process.argv[1] and [2], which removes the env-var prefix.

The Estimate parse keeps only the first number, so '400-800 lines' reads as 400 and '1.2k lines' reads as 1. The size trigger (> 600), and the design it forces, then stay off. Every form now renders an `### Estimate` heading, so this parse runs on every form-filed ticket.

process_issues.description: Skipped review-security: the only executable change is a local dev shell script that passes its arguments to node through env vars, with no trust boundary. Skipped review-workflow-safety: no .github/workflows change. Skipped review-maintainability: off the default roster. Skipped review-spec: there is no --spec and no closing issue reference; the PR body's goal was used only as intent. Dropped a simplicity nit proposing deletion of the grep divergence guard in ticket-check.test.sh: it had no concrete cost, and the task asked for that guard.
